skill.name: appie-chatbot
skill.description: Create, train, and chat with project chatbots via Appie.run. Use when the user asks to create a chatbot, add knowledge or training data, ask a bot a question, check training status, or list chatbots. Triggers include make a chatbot, train bot on this URL, add knowledge, ask the chatbot, chatbot status, list my bots.
skill.summary: Manage Appie.run chatbots, add knowledge sources, check training readiness, and continue conversations through MCP tools.
skill.author: appierun

security_audit.summary: All 35 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, documented service URLs, or application identifiers rather than shell execution or system reconnaissance. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or unauthorized data transfers in the reviewed SKILL.md. The workflow requires authenticated Appie.run access, sends selected knowledge and questions to that service, and discloses per-message credit costs.

content.value_statement: Managing chatbot knowledge and training readiness requires several coordinated steps. This skill guides Appie.run MCP tools through creation, knowledge loading, status checks, and ongoing conversations.
actual_capabilities: Create named project chatbots with optional response instructions, model selection, and temperature settings.
List existing chatbots and their readiness flags.
Add knowledge from text, URLs, sitemaps, or existing Appie article identifiers.
Check training status and wait for readiness before asking questions.
Send questions and reuse session identifiers for follow-up conversations.
Coordinate article-based training with the article-writer skill and optionally use brand context from get_brain.
limitations: Requires an Appie.run project API key and a connected MCP server; it cannot operate offline.
Each ask_chatbot call costs one credit according to the skill documentation.
Answers depend on available knowledge and completed training; the skill does not independently verify their accuracy.
The reviewed package contains instructions only; remote service implementation, availability, and data handling were not verified.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Support Chatbot
use_cases.description: Create a chatbot from approved help pages, check training readiness, and test common customer questions.

use_cases.title: Test Article Knowledge
use_cases.description: Add an existing Appie article as chatbot knowledge and ask questions after training completes.

use_cases.title: Manage Project Chatbots
use_cases.description: Review chatbot readiness, add approved knowledge sources, and continue conversations without losing session context.

prompt_templates.title: List My Chatbots
prompt_templates.prompt: List my Appie.run chatbots with their identifiers and readiness status.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Knowledge Chatbot
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Appie.run chatbot named [name]. Add this approved text as knowledge: [text]. Check training status before asking any questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: create and train a chatbot from supplied text.

prompt_templates.title: Train from a Website
prompt_templates.prompt: Add [approved URL or sitemap] to chatbot [chatbot identifier]. Wait for training readiness, then ask [question]. Report the one-credit question cost.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: load website knowledge and test an answer.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Article-Based Training
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an article about [topic] with appie-article-writer. Once ready, add its article identifier to chatbot [chatbot identifier]. Wait for training, then ask [question].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate article creation, knowledge loading, and a chatbot conversation.

output_examples.input: Show an illustrative chatbot readiness summary.
output: Illustrative result, not a live API response:
Live results include the chatbot identifiers returned by Appie.run.

output_examples.input: Show an illustrative response when I ask a question before training finishes.
output: Illustrative result, not a live API response:
No question was sent to the chatbot.
A question costs one credit once the chatbot is ready.

best_practices: Configure your project API key in the MCP client, never in chat.
Use only knowledge sources approved for transfer to Appie.run.
Confirm the target chatbot, check readiness, and review the credit cost before the first question.
anti_patterns: Uploading confidential or unauthorized material as chatbot knowledge.
Asking questions before training completes or when the chatbot has no knowledge.
Inventing chatbot replies, readiness states, or knowledge sources instead of reporting API results.

faq.question: What do I need before using this skill?
faq.answer: Connect the Appie.run MCP server using your project API key. Configure the key in your client rather than sharing it in chat.

faq.question: Which knowledge sources can I add?
faq.answer: The skill documents text, URLs, sitemaps, and existing Appie article identifiers. URL and sitemap crawling happens in the background.

faq.question: What does each chatbot question cost?
faq.answer: The skill states that each ask_chatbot call costs one credit. Creation, knowledge additions, and training-status checks are documented as free.

faq.question: Can I ask questions while training is running?
faq.answer: No. The workflow checks status and waits until knowledge is ready before sending a question.

faq.question: How are follow-up questions connected?
faq.answer: The workflow reuses the session identifier returned by the chatbot. A new conversation omits that identifier.

faq.question: Does the skill include a chatbot server?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions for Appie.run MCP tools. Chatbot operations depend on the external service and your project access.
